labels.label: T-abs-sc-open-without-tarentin/sc-open-edge
labels.notes: This is a ladder edge, not an ETT label, so there is no paper block. The statements were checked against Causal/Properties.lean (StronglyCausal :105, StronglyCausalOpen :109, CausallyConvexIn :99, CausallyOpen :130, diamond :77) and Causal/Causality.lean (Jplus/Jminus :92/:95). The elaborated signature of StronglyCausal.stronglyCausalOpen_of_causallyOpen is `∀ {M} [TopologicalSpace M] {C : Causality M}, C.CausallyOpen → C.StronglyCausal → C.StronglyCausalOpen`. That is the dispatch's statement exactly. There is no tarentin and no instance argument beyond TopologicalSpace (the file's only `variable` lines are :106 and :110). The weaker forms take what the REPORT says they take. _of_isOpen_Jplus_Jminus takes ∀ O : Opens M, IsOpen (J⁺_⊤ O) ∧ IsOpen (J⁻_⊤ O), which is the roadmap's optional hypothesis. _of_isOpen_hull takes ∀ O, IsOpen (J⁺_⊤ O ∩ J⁻_⊤ O), weaker since J± open implies hull open. exists_opens_causallyConvexIn_of_isOpen_hull is the pointwise core: V ∈ 𝓝 p, CausallyConvexIn V ⊤ and the hull of interior V open give an open W ∋ p with W ⊆ V, causally convex in M. causallyConvexIn_top_iff (`CausallyConvexIn V ⊤ ↔ J⁺_⊤ V ∩ J⁻_⊤ V ⊆ V`) is exactly the definition with U = ⊤. stronglyCausalOpen_iff_stronglyCausal_of_causallyOpen is `C.CausallyOpen → (C.StronglyCausalOpen ↔ C.StronglyCausal)` and needs no tarentin. The old witness StronglyCausal.stronglyCausalOpen (Causal/GlobalHyperbolicity.lean:226, with hT) is untouched. DEC-163: the docstring says the witness takes the two-sided node causally_open (§ 'Which causal openness', :51–61). Witnesses, none vacuous. The timelike line meets every hypothesis. The spacelike line is weak, as disclosed: every subset is causally convex there. The isolated line: isolatedLine_stronglyCausal (:273) is new (no strong-causality lemma for isolatedLine exists in Causal/ or the scaffold) and goes through closed intervals, which are order-convex because ≤_M lies in the order of ℝ (:260). Its causal openness is Causal.isolatedLine_causallyOpen (Causal/LocateExtension.lean:569). It is not tarentin by Causal.tarentin_and_plain_needed (Causal/LocateExtension.lean:687), whose projection .2.1.2.2.1 elaborates to ¬isolatedLine.Tarentin. Mathematically, no diamond J_M(a,b) with a < 0 < b contains 0, so no open diamond does.

labels.label: T-abs-sc-open-without-tarentin/counterexample-shape
labels.notes: StronglyCausal.exists_not_isOpen_hull (:212) says what the REPORT says. From SC and ¬SCO it gives p and N ∈ 𝓝 p with three properties: (i) some open O ∋ p has its hull in N; (ii) every open O ∋ p whose hull lies in N has a non-open hull; (iii) no open W ∋ p with W ⊆ N has hull W ⊆ W. Since W ⊆ hull W always, (iii) is 'W is not its own hull', as the docstring says. This is a conditional characterisation: the REPORT claims no model meets SC ∧ ¬SCO. not_causallyOpen_of_not_stronglyCausalOpen (:233) states ¬CausallyOpen ∧ ¬(∀ O, J±_⊤ O open), the correct contrapositive.

The sharpening is correct: in the proof the open neighbourhood is the hull of ˚J_M(a,b), not the open diamond. It is not a new error claim against the paper. The REPORT's hypothesis row ('strengthened' relative to the paper) is right. The docstring's checklist row disagrees with it (finding 1).

findings.what: The checklist row for prop:GH_fortement_causal (open form) puts `CausallyOpen` in the 'paper hypothesis' column and marks J^±_M-openness '⚠ weakened'. The paper (ETT.tex:1199–1200) assumes only tarentin and global hyperbolicity, Hausdorff from the category, and no causal openness. Against the paper, the Lean form adds J^±_M(O) open, which is '⚠ strengthened' in kb/0006's sense, as the REPORT's own row says ('strengthened'). The docstring and the REPORT disagree, and the docstring compares against the library's form, not the paper. It also quotes no sentence of prop:GH_fortement_causal, though the file says it bears on it. Disclosed elsewhere (partial, unmarked), hence minor.
findings.fix: Rewrite the row as: `prop:GH_fortement_causal`, open form: tarentin, globally hyperbolic, Hausdorff | ✓ carried; ⚠ strengthened: J^±_M(O) open for open O (the paper assumes no causal openness; the library's GloballyHyperbolic.stronglyCausalOpen asks all of CausallyOpen). Add the paper's sentence ('Let M be a tarentin topological spacetime. If M is globally hyperbolic, then M is strongly causal.') to the quote block.

findings.what: 'The hull argument needs the past half of causal openness' (docstring heading) and 'The hull argument needs J⁻-openness' (kb proposal) state a necessity that is not proved. oneWayMembrane_hull_not_isOpen shows that the future half alone does not make the hull open (insufficiency, in one model). The file's own _of_isOpen_hull runs on hull-openness alone, which need not come from J⁻-openness. The REPORT's questions entry and the main theorem's docstring (:185–186) say it exactly ('the future half alone does not open the hull'). Only these two phrasings overreach.
findings.fix: Say 'The future half of causal openness alone does not open the hull' in the heading and in the kb proposal.

membrane: oneWayMembrane_hull_not_isOpen (:295) is checked. Statement: COF ∧ SC ∧ ¬CO ∧ ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 (0,1), CausallyConvexIn V ⊤ ∧ ¬IsOpen (hull (interior V)). The proof takes V = {−1<u<3, 0<v<4, u≤v}, the box intersected with L = {u ≤ v}. V is convex in M because a diamond lies in the product box and a point of R = {v<u} cannot precede b ∈ L (one-way). (1,1) is in the hull: (0,1) ≤_M (1,1) ≤_M (2,3), with (0,1) and (2,3) in ˚V = box ∩ {u<v}. (1+ε/2, 1) ∈ R is not in J⁻_M(˚V), since R is future-closed and ˚V ⊆ L. The REPORT and the docstring both say the membrane is StronglyCausalOpen (oneWayMembrane_stronglyCausalOpen, by balls), so this refutes the argument, not the statement, and they leave SC ∧ COF ⇒ SCO open. That is exactly right, apart from finding 2's phrasing.
keeper_notes: The edge's binders are confirmed: explicit (hO : C.CausallyOpen) (h : C.StronglyCausal), implicit {M} [TopologicalSpace M] {C}, no T0–T3 or other STANDING instance, so standing = [] is right. Emission is an aesop forward rule, so the order of the premises against `from` does not matter (the old edge already has the witness's binders (hT, hO, h) against from = [strongly_causal, tarentin, causally_open]). Lean forms: strongly_causal → Causal.Causality.StronglyCausal, causally_open → Causal.Causality.CausallyOpen, strongly_causal_open → Causal.Causality.StronglyCausalOpen. The matrix does not move. Reasoned from programme/ladder.toml: the reduced edge fires from a node only if the node implies both strongly_causal and causally_open. strongly_causal does not imply causally_open: the notched plane and the one-way membrane are strongly causal and not causally open (the [[open]] note at ~:4049 and the membrane's entries). So (strongly_causal, strongly_causal_open) stays open, and no other pair gains, which the in-memory simulation confirms (0 moved). Until graduation into Causal/, check() reports 'witness not found' for the renamed witness, as the REPORT says.
